title: [Issue]: Broken subtitles: Multiple languages and timestamps mixing up on screen when using chromecast
body:
### Please describe your bug

The issue started happening when upgrading from 10.8.13-1 to 10.9.x (I've confirmed 10.9.3 and 10.9.6 are affected).

Most movies with multiple subtitle tracks are affected, even if there is a bit of randomness to the issue and it does seem to depend, to some extent, on the size of the subtitle files (more details below).

Affected movies work just fine in a web browser or in the Android Client (web player). When playing on these platforms the players display the shiny new "Secondary Subtitle" option introduced in https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-web/pull/3906 ; I have not tested the secondary subtitle feature extensively but it seems to work overall.

*However* when casting from my Android phone to my chromecast, the subtitles are completly broken. It generally starts fine for the first couple of subtitles, then quickly subtitles from multiple language tracks (and generally completely different timestamps) are overlayed directly on top of each other making them unreadable.

Note than when casting I have to select *one* language, and the "Secondary Subtitle" option is not available in the remote control. I suspect this is by design as the secondary subtitle feature was only introduced in the HTML player. However the fact that the bug started appearing on 10.9.x and that it only happens when the secondary subtitle feature is unavailable makes me wonder if this bug could be a side effect of introducing secondary subtitles?

Things I have tried to help gather more information:

- I have tried enabling and disabling the "Allow subtitle extraction on the fly" option on the server. This seems to have no effect on the bug.
- I have ran some experiments by modifying the subtitle files of one particular affected movie. I have not found any particular character or sequence of characters causing the bug. However it seems the issue does not happen (or very rarely) if I almost empty the subtitle files to contain only about 10 subtitles each, it happens very often (though not every time) with the complete subtitle files (about 1100 to 1300 subtitles depending on the language), and it seems somewhat random with intermediary sizes.
- The bug seems very strongly correlated (99 if not 100% of occurrences) with the display of a particular error in the logs: `[ERR] 163 errors encountered while parsing '"srt"' subtitle using the "SubRip" format parser`. I am pasting more complete logs below for the same movie, both when it works and when it does not work.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Environment and config: see below
2. Choose a movie with at least two subtitle tracks, for instance two SRT external subtitle files. Make sure those subtitle files have at least 1500 subtitles each.
3. Open the Android client, connect to a google chrome cast
4. Go to the movie on the Android client, select the first subtitle track
5. Hit play
6. Wait for 1-2 minutes after the first dialogues. Subtitles should break rapidly (randomly not showing, multiple languages and timestamps being overlayed).

### Jellyfin Version

10.9.0

### if other:

_No response_

### Environment

```markdown
- OS:Debian Bookworm
- Linux Kernel: Linux 6.1.0-21-amd64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Debian 6.1.90-1 (2024-05-03) x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Virtualization: None, running directly on Intel NUC
- Clients: Android
- Browser: N/A
- FFmpeg Version: jellyfin-ffmpeg6 6.0.1-7-bookworm
- Hardware Acceleration: Intel QSV
- GPU Model: 
- Plugins: None
- Reverse Proxy: None
- Base URL: N/A
- Networking: Local home network (IPv6)
- Storage: Local NAS
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
So I've been scratching my head for a couple of hours tonight trying to figure this out. I'm trying to confirm my suspicion that the issue was introduced by https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-web/pull/3906

However I'm not getting very far as I lack the most basic understanding of the Jellyfin architecture :<nick>:  The first thing I tried to confirm is whether the PR introduced some changes to the API, but I'm completely baffled by the fact that the whole secondary subtitle feature seems fully self-contained in jellyfin-web and does not seem to affect the server at all? How is that possible when it seems to involve passing an extra parameter to the POST API call [here](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-web/pull/3906/files#diff-b338dd22dfaa8db18edede53fe56aabb5d911c5e611cc33ad3c914410d021cbfR506) ?? :face_with_diagonal_mouth:  Note that the chrome cast code does seem to use the [same API call](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-chromecast/blob/562df52d9b5cdf1a6bf126e494e06b0db217d54a/src/components/jellyfinActions.ts#L289C51-L289C63) (or at least something with a similar name). But if the underlying API wasn't changed there would be no reason for this to break...

It would probably help if @participant1 or @participant15 could take a quick look here as I suspect they would be able to almost instantly confirm whether it is indeed possible that the secondary subtitle change introduced the issue or not.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hey @reporter, I'm not sure if this would be terribly helpful but that `if` clause to add a param in `getPlaybackInfo` that eventually returns `apiClient.getPlaybackInfo(itemId, query, deviceProfile)` isn't actually sending anything off to the server for processing.

When I was building out this feature I was also learning as I went. Essentially just poking around at calls and reverse engineering stuff. You're right to say that the scope of this feature was really limited to the html player and client-side subtitles.

It's been awhile but if I remember correctly, that code you referenced was mainly for fetching after a stream change or coming back after navigating away. If I remember correctly this was involved in saving some sort of state for that? I might be misremembering if `getPlayerState` was just stored locally and maybe `getPlaybackInfo` was used for after returning in a new browser/client session?

It could also be a remnant of the whole dev process and trying to figure stuff out. Maybe I was going down a path and backtracked but ended up leaving that behind? Either way, I can tell you that this was not added with the intent of the server using it, but only for passing back to the client on initial load of the player for some edge case scenarios. But I do feel like I remember that adding that line there solved one of the edge cases and allowed us to fetch the previous state for a new session or something like that. But again, there were multiple ways of saving state all handling different edge cases, so I am not positive.

As you mentioned, this is not (to my knowledge) used in the backend code at all.

If this **_is_** in fact the root cause of the issue you're seeing, I am just as baffled as you are as to why.

Edit: I just wanted to mention again to be clear, the secondary subtitle feature is indeed entirely self contained in the web frontend and more specifically the html player. On top of that, it is scoped only for subtitles handled by the web client. The feature is not available if using any server based subtitles. Nothing is required by the server to make it work. The code you mentioned was to save the index of the target secondary subtitle track only to be returned to the client upon a new browser session. The original idea behind this was to allow it to seamlessly continue playing both subtitles when firing up another session.
But as mentioned earlier, I'd have to dive into the code and debug again to figure out where it is getting picked up. But regardless, it's not being used for any subtitle processing in the server.

In the first example, the transcode reason given in the logs is `ContainerNotSupported`, as it seems chromecast doesn't like the mkv format.

That seems a bit odd as I would expect only remuxing to be needed in that case? However I don't think that's related to the problem. In the three other examples I pasted after that using mp4 (2 working, 1 affected) the transcode reason is logged as `VideoResolutionNotSupported`.

Note that all the examples for which I have pasted logs have been run with "Allow subtitle extractions on the fly" disabled (the default), but I wouldn't expect this to affect subtitles in separate .srt files. I can run the examples again with the option enabled if it helps.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I'm seeing the exact same issue as described by @reporter. It's almost as if all the subtitle streams are getting mixed together and played simultaneously. Sometimes a subtitle will appear in English, then the next line in Dutch, then the next line will appear in 3 different languages overlaid on top of each other, then no subtitles will appear for a few lines, etc.

In my case too, this also seems to have started after upgrading from 10.8.x to 10.9.x. 

PR #10884 caught my eye in that it was merged in 10.9.0 and introduced the ability to extract all subtitle streams simultaneously. Although it could be pure coincidence (and I don't want to imply fault or anything like that), I got a little suspicious just based on the behaviour and description of that PR. I wonder if the author (@participant4) might have any thoughts or be able to help in any way? (Sorry if there is no connection at all @participant4 , at the very least you might know a bit about the internals of subtitle extraction and could maybe point us in the right direction?)

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I have just glanced through the issue. I am not an expert in the whole jellyfin infrastructure, so take everything I say with a grain of salt.

#10884 affects only the extraction of the subtitles from the container. Before the PR, all subtitle streams were extracted in separate `ffmpeg` process calls, after it, it is done with one. We need subtitle extraction, because some clients expect the subtitles to be sent separately, so it can do its own rendering, formatting, etc.

The problem you are experiencing can be caused by multiple layers of this process, I can imagine that there could be a problem in the client's subtitle rendering, but it is possible that the extraction step produced the wrong subtitle file, and the client just renders its content as it was given to it, and other places can be problematic as well, but I am not sure. On the extraction side, I can imagine if we somehow set the output file path to be the same for multiple subtitle streams, this could happen. Before my PR, if the `ffmpeg` commands were executed serially, you would just end up with a fully overwritten subtitle file, but if multiple threads are writing the same file concurrently things like this can happen. It is possible that I have implemented something wrong, or my change surfaced a problem that already existed, or the problem can be somewhere else entirely, sorry if it is the former.

What could really help this investigation is if you could find the extracted and cached subtitle file yourself on your server and could check if it has the correct data or not. I am not sure where the cached files are, but there should be `ffmpeg` logs, which show the path of them. If you find problematic subtitle files, the next step would be to find the log entry about the generation of that file, maybe you can observe the same path for multiple streams problem I mentioned above. However, if the subtitles themselves look like what you would expect it is safe to assume that the problem rises from somewhere else. In the issue description I can see that the subtitles themselves are working with some clients, but not with others, so I think the problem is probably not caused during extraction, but checking these things would help to isolate for sure.

I don't think that I will have the time to reproduce and investigate this problem in the near future, but I can follow the investigation and give hints.

Cheers,
Attila

Just as a quick report, I was able to find the seemingly extracted subtitle files (for me on Windows, in `C:\ProgramData\Jellyfin\Server\data\subtitles\`). It appears that the individual languages are extracted into individual files correctly.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
From @participant5 's experiment above it definitely seems that the `Parse` function [here](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Subtitles/SubtitleEditParser.cs#L46-L63) is flawed in some way. Surely a failure during the call to `LoadSubtitle` should not result in the `subtitle` object being reused in this way.

However I don't understand how this could result in **languages** being mixed up. I don't think this loop iterates over multiple languages, but multiple formats. I suspect that in most cases there is a single format for a given subtitle track? The original implementation of the Parse function did not have this loop (it was introduced in https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/pull/8087).

The sequence of logs in failure cases suggests that there are two parallel / asynchronous executions of this loop, but each execution iterates a single time through the loop body, for instance:
[2024-06-28 09:30:42.116 +01:00] [DBG] charset "utf-8" detected for "/path/to/library/MovieName.720p.x264.en.srt"
[2024-06-28 09:30:42.122 +01:00] [DBG] Trying to parse '"srt"' subtitle using the "SubRip" format parser [**Loop body begins, line 48**]
[2024-06-28 09:30:42.129 +01:00] [DBG] charset "iso-8859-1" detected for "/path/to/library/<redacted-host>.srt"
[2024-06-28 09:30:42.133 +01:00] [DBG] Trying to parse '"srt"' subtitle using the "SubRip" format parser [**Again, loop body begins, line 48**]
[2024-06-28 09:30:42.150 +01:00] [ERR] 120 errors encountered while parsing '"srt"' subtitle using the "SubRip" format parser [**Loop body ends, line 58**]
[2024-06-28 09:30:42.156 +01:00] [ERR] 120 errors encountered while parsing '"srt"' subtitle using the "SubRip" format parser [**Again loop body ends at line 58**]

I'm wondering if there is something in the code of this `Parse` method (or within the code of libse that it calls) that does not support multithreaded / asynchronous execution correctly?

comments.author: participant10
comments.body:
I have this problem as well, also on the Android TV Jellyfin app.

I was able to work around it (at least, that's how it seems for now) by doing the following:
1. Disabling the builtin on-the-fly subtitle extraction in the Admin panel as described in https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/issues/12113#issuecomment-2553583428
2. *Disabling* (not enabling) the Subtitle Extract plugin, which I already had installed.
3. Manually deleting the subtitle cache at `$JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR/subtitles`.
4. Restarting the server.

This seems to have fixed it for me, though at the cost of a small delay (~10s) on video startup.

I wonder if the only reason this works is because the subtitle cache miss triggers some better behaved code path, and I suspect that replaying the same video would repro the bug again, but I haven't been able to verify this.

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
Came here to say +1; this has become a very annoying, borderline deal-breaker bug for me since I have no (satisfactory) workarounds, and working subtitles often aren't optional for my family and I. As time goes on, I'm becoming more desperate for a solution, but it's a shame really because I love Jellyfin, and this _used_ to work flawlessly.

I discovered this issue _around_ the same time this issue was posted, maybe a bit earlier. I first thought maybe it was just a sporadic quirk possibly stemming from corrupt media or transient resource contention issues, but after I realized it was becoming consistent and affecting all media, I started searching and found this issue. I can't recall for certain if it was introduced by upgrading to 10.9.x, but it aligns with the timeline.

I'm currently running 10.10.3, and this is still an issue.

A while back, I attempted to downgrade from 10.9.x (which was current at the time) to 10.8.x as a workaround, only to find out that it was not practical (nothing was backwards compatible, neither server data nor clients, between 10.9.x and 10.8.x).

The only (unsatisfactory) workarounds I've found are:

1. Playing / streaming jellyfin on my android phone, and screencasting (e.g. screen-mirroring) to my TV + Chromecast. The android client is capable of natively decoding and rendering embedded subtitles, and so isn't impacted by this issue. This works better than I would have anticipated, but it still has many flaws that make it unsatisfactory.
2. Preemptively re-encoding media using tools like Handbrake with subtitle burn-in enabled. This does make the playback experience as good as it was before this bug, but at the cost of being very tedious / time-consuming to perform manually, and (since I like to preserve originals) doubles the storage requirements.

Doesn't this trigger transcoding (to burn-in the subtitles, since you've now disabled all paths for extraction to occur)? That would likely fix the issue of course, as the burn in is performed server-side, but would only work in scenarios where the server is capable of full real-time transcoding -- unfortunately this isn't practical in my case (I run the server on an older Synology DS415+ -- it can *almost* keep up with x264 1080p, but it's just a tad too slow for reliable on-the-fly transcoding).

Tangent: Although simply fixing the bug that is the subject of this issue thread would be the most desirable outcome, it makes me think that (automated) management of preemptive _offline_ transcoding to preferred codecs / formats might be a nice (future) feature for Jellyfin, as it would have practical applications for myself and many others that run servers incapable of reliable on-the-fly transcoding beyond just presenting yet another workaround for this bug.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Just an idea:

Maybe libse's SubtitleFormat::LoadSubtitle method is stateful (not thread safe), and the Parse  https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding%2FSubtitles%2FSubtitleEditParser.cs#L36 method is using the same SubtitleFormat instances from multiple threads.

This would explain loading the srt file to Subtitle Edit (using libse) successfully, but failing to do so in Jellyfin.

On why it only happened now, I think changing the subtitle renderer in jellyfin-androidtv 0.18.0 might have resulted in calling some functions that have not been called before (or have not been called from multiple threads before), just a guess, though.

All of these are open source, so we can check, I will try to do so in a couple of days after the holidays.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Thanks @participant13 for checking this out!

@participant10 We could cache the classes instead of the instances to a `_subtitleFormatTypes`  map, then lookup the class and create one new instance in `Parse()`. This would have minimal performance impact compared to the code on main, namely one constructor call. With @participant13 's PoC we iterate though and instantiate all available `SubtitleFormat`s for each `Parse()` call, which can be significantly slower.
